subject: Launch traffic guardrails & quota request — Thunderbolt.ai May launch
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch traffic guardrails & quota request — Thunderbolt.ai May launch

Team —

Heads up: Thunderbolt.ai confirmed their go-live window for the North America pilot on 2027-05-10 (public launch 2027-05-17). They shared an updated traffic forecast (attached: traffic_forecast_v2.xlsx). High-level ask: temporary quota bump + traffic guardrail checks for the first 72 hours of the pilot.

Quick summary of what Thunderbolt expects at peak (from last sync):
- Peak RPS: 180 requests/sec (30s bursty fan-out lasting ~60s every 3–5 minutes during user onboarding flows)
- Avg tokens per request: 420 (prompt + expected responses)
- Model family: open-llama-70b-ish for primary flows, fallback to quantized 13B for lower-tier routes
- Region: us-west initially with failover to us-east

Immediate asks for this thread:
1) Neha — can infra provide a temporary quota increase for TB (both token and concurrency limits) for the pilot window: 2027-05-10 00:00 — 2027-05-13 23:59 PT? We need a rough RPS->token mapping and a plan for auto-fallback when dedicated capacity saturates.
2) Jonas / Product — what guardrails can we enable to protect latency SLOs (per-route throttles, prioritized routing, KV-cache pinning)?
3) Karthik / Marissa — I need any procurement/contract blockers from their side (SLA/penalty asks, billing contact).

Attachments: traffic_forecast_v2.xlsx (spread by hour; includes token mix scenarios A/B).

I'll consolidate answers and file a formal quota change request once we have numbers.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch traffic guardrails & quota request — Thunderbolt.ai May launch

Thanks Marcus — good summary. A few clarifying questions before I can approve a temporary quota bump and propose exact numbers:

1) Traffic shape: are the 180 RPS spikes evenly distributed across routes, or concentrated on a small subset (e.g., /generate vs /chat)? If it's concentrated, we should set per-route caps instead of a blanket concurrency increase.
2) Token mix: the 420 tokens/request — is that average for both prompt + response? If A/B scenarios differ (A=350, B=520), include both.
3) Model mapping: confirm which routes must hit the open-llama variant vs which can use quantized 13B fallback.
4) Canary ramp cadence: do we want a stepped ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100% over 90 minutes) or an all-up ramp? Recommend stepped so we can observe KV-cache warm-up and cold-start latency.

Notes on constraints and recommended guardrails:
- We can grant a token-cap increase scoped to the TB account for the 72-hour window, but it needs explicit start/end times and a single owner for de-escalation (ops pager).
- Per-route throttles + prioritization is doable; we should pin KV-cache entries for their top 15 prompt templates to avoid early churn.
- If a single route exceeds 200 RPS for >2 minutes, automated fallback to 13B should trigger with a notification to the TB LaunchOps channel.

I'll prototype a quota-change request doc (to be signed by Finance) once Marcus confirms the exact split and the ramp plan. Also linking an internal runbook for burst-handling: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/burst-handling

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

Adding context from the commercial side:
- Thunderbolt is asking for an SLA of 99.9% for the pilot window and an explicit exception to our default throttling for the first 48 hours (they want an elevated retry budget). We should avoid long-term SLA commitments but can offer a pilot SLA as part of the launch package.
- Procurement asks: they need an invoice for the pilot committed capacity and a statement of expected outage/fallback behavior for their compliance team. Marissa — can you draft the one-page addendum?
- Customer contact: looping in Sana (cc'd in my next note) for final confirmation on traffic shape.

If we can get a scoped quota bump with per-route guardrails and a documented fallback, we can sign the pilot addendum today.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Launch traffic guardrails & quota request — Thunderbolt.ai May launch

Thanks all — confirming the numbers from our side. We ran internal load tests over the weekend and observed:
- Sustained baseline during onboarding flows: ~60 RPS
- Short fan-out bursts up to ~220 RPS for 40–70s when power-users onboard (this happens ~once every 4–6 minutes)
- Avg tokens/request: 400–460 depending on prompt path; some diagnostic requests hit ~800 tokens

Model usage plan: production will hit open-llama-70b for premium customers (roughly 55% of requests) and quantized 13B for the rest. We can accept a stepped canary (25/50/100 over 60 minutes) as long as we have an option to pause the ramp.

Attaching our CDN traffic plan and a short appendix with time-of-day user curves (cdn-traffic-plan.pdf).

Sana Patel
Head of Product, Thunderbolt.ai
sana@thunderbolt.ai

Subject: Re: Launch traffic guardrails & quota request — Thunderbolt.ai May launch

Thanks — this is actionable. Below is the proposed plan I want to lock in by EOD so we can route the quota-change paperwork tomorrow:

Proposed pilot guardrail + quota plan (summary):
- Scope: TB account (id TB-2027-0421) — temporary increases from 2027-05-10 00:00 PT -> 2027-05-13 23:59 PT.
- Token capacity: provision for sustained 120 RPS @ 420 tokens + 2x headroom for bursts (i.e., capacity target = tokens/sec for 240 RPS) — Neha/Infra to confirm exact token/sec mapping.
- Concurrency caps: per-route throttle of 220 RPS; automated fallback to quantized 13B if route latency > 1.2s p95 for >3 minutes.
- Canary ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 60 minutes with an ops hold at each step (manual go/no-go).
- Observability: enable per-token cost tracing + early-warning alerts for sustained 80% token utilization.
- De-escalation owner: Laura Bennett (ops) — pager on-call contact to be added to the LaunchOps channel.

Action items:
- Neha: draft the quota_change_request.pdf and confirm token/sec numbers (today EOD).
- Jonas: confirm which guardrail knobs are product-managed vs infra-managed and list any rollout limitations.
- Marissa/Karthik: prepare pilot addendum and invoice; Marissa to draft addendum today.
- Marcus: will open the HubSpot deal and attach forecast + doc links (link in metadata).

If everyone agrees, I will file the formal request and loop Finance for sign-off.

— Marcus
